title: Closed points have affine basic neighbourhoods under ideal H1 vanishing
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] such that $H^1(X,\mathcal I)=0$ for every quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ [pqf-def-coherent, pqf-def-cohomology]. For every point $x\in X$ whose singleton is closed, there is $f\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ with $x\in X_f$ and $X_f$ affine. Here $X_f$ is the locus where the germ of $f$ is a unit.

source.place: Tag 01XF, label lemma-quasi-compact-h1-zero-covering; first paragraph of proof, lines 323-352

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $x$, and its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. Put $Z=X\setminus U$ and $Z\prime=Z\cup\{x\}$. The reduced-induced construction gives quasi-coherent ideals $\mathcal I\prime\subseteq\mathcal I$ defining $Z\prime$ and $Z$. Their restrictions to $U$ are $\mathfrak m$ and $A$, and their restrictions to $X\setminus\{x\}$ agree.

The quotient $\mathcal I/\mathcal I\prime$ restricts to $\widetilde{A/\mathfrak m}$ on $U$ and zero on $X\setminus\{x\}$. Gluing over these two opens gives global sections $A/\mathfrak m$. The long exact sequence and the assumed vanishing of $H^1(X,\mathcal I\prime)$ lift its section $1$ to $f\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal I)$.

Viewed as a structure-sheaf section, $f$ vanishes on $Z$ and its residue at $x$ is $1$. Hence $x\in X_f\subseteq U$. The basic-open construction identifies $X_f$ with $D(f|_U)$ in the affine scheme $U$, so it is affine.
